children: Wedbush Securities thinks the recovery in the movie theater sector will continue as a normalized film pipeline, premium-format demand, and higher customer spending lift revenue, margins, and free cash flow even if attendance never returns to historical peaks.

Notably, the Q3 North American box office reached a record $3.03B, up 28% year over year and above comparable quarters in 2018–2019. Following the strong quarter, Wedbush raised its full-year 2026 box-office forecast to $10.5B from $10.0B, representing 21% growth. For 2027, analyst Alicia Reese and her team expect a further 2% increase in the North America box office to approximately $10.6B. The solid 2027 movie slate includes
Reese highlighted that consumers increasingly pay for IMAX

and other premium screens while spending more on concessions and merchandise. Those trends allow operators to generate more revenue per attendee. Longer theatrical windows, increased output from technology companies, and Netflix’s planned wide releases are seen providing additional support.
The firm remains bullish on AMC Entertainment
, slotting all three with Outperform ratings.

title: Wedbush lifts 2026 North American box office forecast, points to solid 2027 film slate
